title: Peak Overlap
statement:
A conference hall hosts talks. `talks[i] = [start, end]` means talk `i` runs from time `start` up to, but **not including**, time `end`. So a talk ending at time `t` does not overlap a talk starting at time `t`.

Return the **largest number of talks running at the same moment**.
constraints: talks[i] has exactly two numbers [start, end]

examples.explanation: At time 2 and 3 two talks run. At time 4 the first has ended and two others run.
Each talk ends exactly when the next begins, so they never overlap.

hints.nudge: The number of running talks only changes when a talk starts or ends. What if you looked at those moments in order?
hints.pattern: Sort the start times and the end times separately, then sweep through them.
hints.walkthrough: Checking every start time against every talk is O(n^2). Instead, split the talks into two sorted lists: all start times and all end times. Sweep forward: when the next start is earlier than the earliest unfinished end, a talk begins, so the count goes up; otherwise a talk ends first, so the count goes down. Because a talk ending at time t frees the room for one starting at t, ends win ties (the check is 'start < end', not '<='). Track the maximum count seen. O(n log n) from the sorting.
